title: Renewal of a Lease Agreement
requirement: Landlords of residential rental properties, excluding owner-occupied two or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, or transient/seasonal units, must have good cause to refuse to renew a lease.
coverage_conditions: residential rental properties excluding owner-occupied two or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, or transient/seasonal units
exemptions: owner-occupied two or three-family dwellings, motels, hotels, transient or seasonal units
quoted_span: No landlord of residential rental properties except those in owner occupied two or three family dwellings, motels or hotels, transient, or seasonal units may fail to renew any lease, regardless of whether it is written or oral unless they have good cause not to renew the lease.

title: Maximum Security Deposit
requirement: The maximum security deposit a landlord can collect from a tenant cannot exceed one and one-half times one month's rent.
coverage_conditions: most residential rental properties, including mobile homes
quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

title: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 Maximum Security Deposit
requirement: The maximum security deposit a landlord may collect cannot exceed one and one-half times one month's rent. Any advanced rents or prepaid funds held to secure future rents, including the last month's rent, are considered part of the security deposit.
exemptions: owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling (unless the tenant makes the provision applicable after 30 days written notice)
quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

title: N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 Deposit Account and Interest
requirement: Landlords receiving security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit the funds in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account. Landlords with 10 or more units have the option of investing in an insured money market fund or a variable rate account in a New Jersey bank. All interest or earnings belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited toward rent.
exemptions: security deposits for seasonal use or rental (term of not more than 125 consecutive days)
quoted_span: A landlord or designee who receives security deposit money for ten or less units must deposit that money in an insured bank or savings and loan association located in New Jersey in an interest-bearing account at the current interest rate at the time of deposit.

title: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1 Return of Security Deposit
requirement: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit plus interest less allowable deductions. If a landlord fails to return the deposit within 30 days or wrongfully withholds an amount, the tenant may sue for double the amount plus court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

title: N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h) Law Against Discrimination
requirement: Landlords and rental agencies are prohibited from refusing to rent or discriminating in housing units based on race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
exemptions: two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex
quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.

title: Credit Checks and Background Checks
requirement: Landlords are allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the credit report and may request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report.

title: Late Fee and Grace Period for Seniors and Specific Benefit Recipients
requirement: Certain senior citizens and recipients of specific governmental pensions, disability benefits, or assistance must be given a five-business-day grace period for rent due on the first of the month without delinquency or late charges assessed.
quoted_span: Any senior citizen receiving a Social Security Old Page Pension, a Railroad Retirement Pension, or any other governmental pension in lieu of a Social Security Old Age Pension, and any recipients of Social Security Disability Benefits, Supplemental Security Income, or benefits under Work First New Jersey, must be given a period of five (5) business days grace period for payment when the rent is due on the first of the month.

title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Exemption
requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction.
quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

title: Condominium and Cooperative Conversion Rent Increases
requirement: When a building is converted to a condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased solely to cover costs resulting from the conversion.
coverage_conditions: buildings converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units
quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

title: Anti-Eviction Act - General Good Cause Requirement
requirement: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether written or oral, without good cause, and the landlord must prove in court that grounds for eviction exist.
coverage_conditions: most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, complexes, and rooming and boarding homes
exemptions: two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (unless the occupant has no alternate residence and resides there continually); a unit held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family if that family member is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the dwelling unit.
quoted_span: The Anti-Eviction Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect blameless tenants from eviction and was adopted in recognition of the housing shortage in the State.

title: Failure to Pay Rent Increase
requirement: A landlord may file an eviction suit if a tenant fails to pay a rent increase, provided the rent increase is not unconscionable and complies with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control, and a Notice to Quit is served at least one month prior.
quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.

title: Illegal Occupancy Relocation Assistance
requirement: Tenants evicted for illegal occupancy are entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times their monthly rent, payable by the landlord at least five days before removal.
quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

title: Retirement of Property from Residential Use
requirement: Landlords seeking to permanently retire a building from residential use must serve a Notice to Quit at least 18 months prior to filing for eviction, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction.

title: Refusal to Accept Reasonable Lease Changes
requirement: Landlords may evict tenants who refuse reasonable, substantial changes to lease terms upon expiration, provided a one-month Notice to Quit is served.
quoted_span: When the lease expires, the landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes to the terms and conditions of the lease.

title: Habitual Late Payment of Rent
requirement: Landlords may evict for habitual late payment of rent after serving a Notice to Cease and a one-month Notice to Quit.
quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

title: Conversion to Condominium or Cooperative
requirement: Landlords converting properties to condominiums or cooperatives must serve a three-year Notice to Quit before filing for eviction.
coverage_conditions: properties converting to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of two or more dwelling units
exemptions: senior citizen tenant or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status
quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction.

title: Reprisal Against Tenants
requirement: Landlords are prohibited from evicting, altering lease terms, or refusing to renew a lease in reprisal for a tenant exercising civil rights, such as enforcing lease rights or complaining to government authorities.
coverage_conditions: all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes
quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights

title: New Jersey Foreclosure Fairness Act
requirement: When a new owner of a foreclosed property makes a bona fide monetary offer to induce a tenant to vacate, they are prohibited from using pressure tactics, including increasing rent in excess of any applicable rent control ordinance or, if not subject to rent control, imposing an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.
quoted_span: An increase in rent in excess of any rent control or rent leveling ordinance, or if the property is not subject to rent control, an unreasonable or unconscionable rent increase.
